summary: Hosted service, quality sprint: fixes from scoring four private reference applications on 2026-10-29. The Standard writer (Claude Opus 5.5) has a 64,000-token output cap, so a full draft no longer stops at the old 32,768-token cap. A provider call the service rejects after it was billed, such as a draft cut off at its cap, now counts in the run's cost, its cost limit and the usage reads. New hosted workspaces start with autopilot on, so a run revises through blocking findings up to its round limit, and the web screen's Autopilot checkbox turns it off. The coverage judge credits a draft that shows a behavioural or seniority requirement through concrete work, and a nice-to-have requirement weighs half in relevance. New runs use author prompt cli-author-v17, which writes a full two-page CV and keeps accomplishments over wording. Run details show the writing policy a hosted run used.
knownLimitations: Staging only: production keeps its earlier images until the owner deploys this tag there. Existing workspaces keep autopilot off until it is turned on. The draft quality changes are measured by a re-score of the four references after this release; until then the Balanced draft is not yet shown to be sendable. The cost of a complete cached run is still to measure (#1597).
